newsitem.title: USA: Fed expected to add reserves via term system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed expected to add reserves via term system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to add reserves to the banking system on Thursday through overnight or term system repurchase agreements, analysts said.
"We expect the Fed to intervene with system repos," said analysts at MMS International.
"The Fed has a little add need that remains," said James Glassman, senior economist at Chase Securities Inc. "Part of the add need is caused by Treasury baances running a little high."
Glassman said the Fed could do a four-day system repurchase agreement or could choose an overnight system RP.
"They have shown a preference for doing overnight repos, playing it day by day," he said.
Glassman said tax inflows could be surprisingly strong.

"The Fed will have a big job at the end of the month because there is potential for tax and loan accounts at the Fed to fill up and spill over into the Treasury's account at the Fed," he said. "If the Treasury's balance at the Fed surges at the end of the month, that would have the effect of draining reserves from the banking system."
Glassman said it was early to make a judgement, but that tax flows look strong.
"The economy has been strong," he explained. "Corporate porifts have been quite strong."
Federal funds were trading at 5-7/16 percent, just below the 5-1/2 percent target rate, at mid-morning.
